Combat Rogue

WoW: Forever · Melee DPS · Updated November 13, 2026 · Client build 1.60.1.70938 · Null Ossuary

Written for the live game, levels 1 to 60. Talent rows unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40, a level later for each point spent in another tree. Talent effects are Blizzard's November 2 notes; trained ranks and costs are read from the client, build 1.60.1.70938. Blizzard has not changed Rogue since launch beyond two tooltip fixes on November 6. The builds are Icy Veins' (updated November 4), Wowhead's (November 6 and 11) and WoWSims' presets, each named. Nothing about level 60 is measured: no raid opens before December 9. If a tooltip on this page differs from the text, go by the text.

What Combat is for

Steady damage from whatever weapon you are holding, with three talents that change how a fight goes. RiposteRiposteTalentCastInstantCost10 EnergyRangeMeleeCooldown6 sec cooldownDuration6 sec at 20 costs 10 Energy after a parry, for 150% weapon damage and a 6-second disarm, on a 6-second cooldown. Blade FlurryBlade FlurryLevel 1 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantCost25 EnergyCooldown120 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases your melee attack speed by 20% and your melee attacks strike an additional nearby opponent. Lasts 15 sec. at 30 costs 25 Energy for +20% melee speed and one extra nearby target for 15 seconds, on a 2-minute cooldown. Adrenaline RushAdrenaline RushSpell · PhysicalCastInstantCooldown300 sec cooldownDuration15 secIncreases your Energy regeneration rate by 100% for 15 sec. at 40 doubles Energy regeneration for 15 seconds, on a 5-minute cooldown.

Blizzard's own framing is "hard hitting direct damage and little bit of cleave damage with Blade Flurry". Icy Veins, updated November 9, calls it "some of the highest sustained single-target damage output in the game" and "the only Rogue specialization that can cleave". Wowhead's levelling page, updated November 6, says Combat Rogues "feel very smooth to level with", and its overview gives the reason the spec travels well: it does "not rely on Poisons or Bleed effects", which some enemies are immune to.

Both sites build their levelling around RiposteRiposteTalentCastInstantCost10 EnergyRangeMeleeCooldown6 sec cooldownDuration6 sec. Icy Veins takes DeflectionDeflectionTalent · Rank 3 of 3CastInstantIncreases your Parry chance by 6%. and RiposteRiposteTalentCastInstantCost10 EnergyRangeMeleeCooldown6 sec cooldownDuration6 sec by level 20. Wowhead: "This will be the bread and butter for Combat Rogues while leveling."

Lasts 20 sec., a 40% crit bonus on your next builder for 20 seconds after a kill. Icy Veins leaves it until 45 and gets each milestone talent two levels sooner. Gaunerh, levelling at launch, skips it too because he does not want to be hurried from one enemy to the next; his order otherwise matches Icy Veins' milestones.

Stat priority

While levelling, from Icy Veins: weapon damage, then Hit and Expertise, Agility, critical strike, Strength, Stamina. Both sites' Sinister StrikeSinister StrikeLevel 1 · Spell · Physical · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost45 EnergyRangeMeleeAn instant strike that causes 3 damage in addition to your normal weapon damage. Awards 1 combo point. builds assume a slow main hand.

At 60 the two sites order the top differently, and both say it is early.

  • Icy Veins: Expertise to 6.5%, Hit to 8%, Agility, weapon damage, critical strike.
  • Wowhead, which calls its own list "purely speculative for endgame": Hit to 8%, Expertise to 6.5%, weapon skill, then Hit on to 17% for poisons, Agility, critical strike.
  • WoWSims' stored weights put Expertise and Hit first, then Agility, then Haste and critical strike level with each other. They were not retuned after the November 3 talent rework (WoWSims' model).

  • Mace: the armour ignore applies to both weapons, even with a mace in only one hand.

At level 60

In a group you are single-target damage, one cooldown of cleave, and control. Icy Veins, updated November 9: Combat "is likely to find a spot in parties forming for any kind of content", and its contribution on trash packs is "sadly very limited". Wowhead expects most Rogues to keep a Combat spec beside another one now that dual specialisation exists.

The weapon question has a first answer in Wowhead's Hack and SlashHack and SlashTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantGives your melee weapon attacks a benefit depending on the weapon. Axe/Sword: Your successful melee attacks have a 5% chance to trigger an extra attack on the target. Dagger/Fist: Increases your critical strike chance by 5%. Mace: Your attacks ignore 15% of your target's armor. notes above. What is not known yet is how the sword and dagger builds compare on real bosses: that waits for logs, and the first raids open on December 9.
